modules.title: Design scalable and loosely coupled architectures

nodes.title: Stateful vs stateless; horizontal vs vertical scaling

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: How do state placement and scaling direction affect architecture?

reveal.text: A stateless application tier keeps user/session state outside individual compute instances, so any healthy instance can handle the next request. Horizontal scaling adds more instances (scale out), while vertical scaling makes one instance larger (scale up).

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: Reveal each row and compare neighboring architecture choices.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
What is Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?

glossary.definition: A design where one server does not need to remember request or session state locally, so another healthy server can handle the next request.
A design where a server keeps state that later requests depend on, such as local session data.
Adding more instances or workers. This is also called scaling out.
Making one instance larger. This is also called scaling up.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Elastic Load Balancing distributes requests across healthy targets, and EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances to match demand.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When should ELB and Auto Scaling appear together?

items: Traffic must be spread across multiple healthy targets.
Compute capacity should grow and shrink with demand.
Unhealthy instances should be replaced while traffic stays on healthy targets.

reveal.text: Amazon SQS durably buffers messages so producers and consumers do not need to run at the same rate or be available at the same time. Standard queues use an at-least-once delivery model, so consumers should tolerate duplicates.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Which architecture signal strongly points to SQS?

items: Producer traffic can spike faster than workers can process it.
Work must wait durably while consumers are slow or unavailable.
A worker should retry failed work without making the producer stay synchronous.

items: One event must reach multiple independent subscribers.
The publisher should not call every downstream consumer directly.
For durable independent processing, SNS can fan out to separate SQS queues.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: AWS Lambda runs event-driven code without managing servers and scales concurrent execution in response to incoming work within service limits.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When is Lambda a strong compute choice?

items: Short-lived event-driven code should run without managing servers.
The workload can scale through concurrent function invocations.
Check concurrency/service quotas when a large burst must be handled reliably.

items: Fargate: run supported ECS/EKS containers without managing worker servers.

nodes.title: API Gateway for loosely coupled APIs

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Amazon API Gateway provides managed endpoints for REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs and integrates with backends such as Lambda or private services.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Which requirement points to API Gateway?

items: A managed REST, HTTP, or WebSocket API front door is required.
API-level auth, throttling, routing, or managed backend integration matters.
Compare with ALB when the main need is load balancing rather than API management.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE

items: API Gateway for loosely coupled APIs

Limiting request rate to protect capacity or enforce a service limit.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Where can caching remove repeated work?

reveal.text: Caching keeps frequently reused data closer to the caller. CloudFront caches content at edge locations, ElastiCache provides general in-memory application caching, and DAX is a DynamoDB-focused cache.

glossary.definition: A faster temporary copy of data kept closer to where it is needed.
A request answered from the cache without fetching the original source.
A request whose data is not currently in the cache.
Time to live. How long cached data remains valid before it expires or is refreshed.

nodes.title: Object, block, and file storage selection

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What is the object vs block vs file mental model?

reveal.text: Amazon S3 is object storage, Amazon EBS provides block storage for compute such as EC2, and Amazon EFS provides a managed shared file system that multiple Linux clients can mount.

What is Amazon EFS?

glossary.definition: Storage that keeps data as objects addressed by keys rather than as a mounted disk.
Storage presented as raw blocks to a host, similar to a virtual disk.
Storage presented with file-system semantics such as files and directories.

modules.title: Design highly available and/or fault-tolerant architectures

nodes.title: RDS Multi-AZ DB instance/cluster vs read replicas

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: An RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment uses a standby for high availability and automatic failover; that standby does not serve reads. An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster has a writer and two readable standby instances across three AZs. Separate read replicas primarily scale reads and use asynchronous replication.

prompts.label: COMPARE
prompts.placeholder: The choices are visible. Reveal the differences one cell at a time.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: DB instance standby -> HA, not read scaling

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
Multi-AZ deployments for Amazon RDS
Multi-AZ DB cluster deployments for Amazon RDS
Working with DB instance read replicas

glossary.definition: Switching service to a healthy standby or alternate resource when the primary becomes unavailable.
A database replica that can serve read traffic and is commonly used to scale reads.
Replication where a write waits for required replica-side work before completion.
Replication where the source can complete a write before the replica has fully applied the change.

nodes.title: Availability Zones and Regions as failure domains

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Availability Zones are isolated locations within a Region, and using multiple AZs reduces exposure to a single-AZ failure.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When do multiple AZs or multiple Regions matter?

items: Multiple AZs reduce exposure to a single-AZ failure.
Multiple Regions are used when the requirement includes Region-level DR or geographic separation.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

items: Availability Zones and Regions as failure domains

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

An isolated location within an AWS Region.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Amazon Route 53 routing policies can direct users among endpoints, and health-aware policies can stop returning unhealthy targets when configured appropriately.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When is health-aware DNS failover useful?

items: A primary and secondary endpoint need DNS-based failover.
DNS answers should consider endpoint health according to the configured policy.
Do not assume unhealthy always means Route 53 returns no record; behavior depends on configuration.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: RPO is the maximum acceptable data-loss window, while RTO is the maximum acceptable outage/recovery time. Backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, and multi-site active-active trade increasing steady-state cost and complexity for faster recovery.

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: Recovery point objective. The maximum recent data loss the business can tolerate, measured in time.
Recovery time objective. The maximum time the workload can remain unavailable before recovery.
A DR design that keeps critical core components ready while much of the compute is started or scaled during recovery.
A DR design that keeps a smaller but functional copy of the workload running in the recovery location.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Replication improves availability or locality by maintaining additional copies, while backups preserve recoverable historical points.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When do you need replication versus a backup?

items: Replication maintains another current copy for availability, locality, or DR.
Backups preserve historical recovery points for deletion, corruption, ransomware, or operator mistakes.
A bad change can also be replicated, so replication is not automatically a historical backup.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: Maintaining another copy of data by sending changes from a source to another location.
A stored state that can be used to restore data or a resource to an earlier point.

nodes.title: RDS Proxy and database connection resilience

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Amazon RDS Proxy pools and reuses connections to supported RDS/Aurora databases. It is useful when bursty applications create many short-lived connections that would otherwise consume excessive database connection capacity.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: What scenario should make RDS Proxy stand out?

items: Lambda or other bursty workloads create many short-lived DB connections.
The database is spending excessive resources managing client connections.
The design needs connection pooling/reuse and improved connection resilience.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
Amazon RDS Proxy concepts and terminology

glossary.definition: A reusable group of database connections shared by application requests.
A condition where an application creates more database connections than the database can safely support.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What should this concept make you think of?

reveal.text: Immutable infrastructure replaces unhealthy or outdated instances from versioned images or templates instead of manually repairing servers in place.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: When is replacement better than in-place repair?

items: Instances should be recreated from a known image/template rather than manually patched into different states.
A failed or outdated node can be terminated and replaced automatically.
Versioned images/templates make fleet consistency and rollback easier.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What phrase should make this answer jump out?

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide

glossary.definition: An operating model where unhealthy or outdated servers are replaced from known images or templates instead of repaired manually in place.

nodes.title: Service quotas, throttling, and failover capacity

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Why can an otherwise-correct failover design still fail?

reveal.text: AWS services have resource and request-rate quotas. A secondary Region or account must have enough quota headroom for the expected failover load or scaling/API requests can be blocked or throttled.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: What should be checked before relying on failover?

items: Check quotas in every Region/account that can receive production failover traffic.
Request increases before an incident when the secondary environment cannot support expected scale.
Monitor quota use and request-rate throttling as part of resilience planning.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Which wording points to quota planning?

source_refs.title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03) exam guide
Manage service quotas across accounts and Regions
Ensure sufficient quota headroom for failover

glossary.definition: A limit on resources or request rates for an AWS service in an account or Region.
Unused quota capacity reserved for growth, bursts, or failover.
Rejecting or slowing requests because a request-rate or capacity limit was reached.

prompts.label: WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: What does tracing show that one service metric cannot?

reveal.text: AWS X-Ray traces requests through participating components of a distributed application. Traces and the service map help identify where latency, errors, and dependency failures occur.

prompts.label: WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Which troubleshooting requirement points to X-Ray?

items: One request crosses several microservices and the slow/failing dependency must be identified.
The problem cannot be isolated from one host or aggregate metric.
The architecture needs request-level traces and service-to-service visibility.

prompts.label: EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: What wording should trigger distributed tracing?

AWS X-Ray concepts

glossary.definition: A record that follows one request through participating components of a distributed application.
X-Ray trace data describing work performed by one participating service or component.
A visual view of traced application components and their connections.
